scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9112: From my machine PC0 (20.1.1.10) I can no longer reach
PC12 (120.1.1.10) at all -- my pings time out, every single one. It was fine
before last night, so something has changed on your side. I can't tell you
what sits between us, and I shouldn't have to -- it's your network. Check the
path and get us talking again today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) end
  to end with 0% loss, traversing the full OSPF backbone (areas 0-4 + virtual-links)
  and the EIGRP domain (r11/r12/r13). Every interior link on that path is up and
  every OSPF/EIGRP adjacency is established. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone link-down that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12 at
all because an interior link is down -- is NOT reproducible: PC0 (20.1.1.10) pings
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss in both directions. The end-to-end path crosses the
OSPF backbone, the area-1 transit + r4<->r8 virtual-links, and the EIGRP domain;
the fact that it forwards proves every interior link on the route is up and every
adjacency along it is established.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-network reachability is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
ping, finds it working at 0% loss, optionally traces the path or spot-checks a
couple of OSPF/EIGRP neighbor states (all up), and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a down interior link -- picking some backbone interface and declaring it
the cut to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The user's reported symptom — PC0 (20.1.1.10) unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.10) — is not confirmed by any live evidence. A topology-wide reachability probe measured 0% packet loss in both directions, with sub-millisecond RTT, ruling out any active data-plane failure.

The PC0→PC12 forwarding path was traced in full. PC0 sends traffic via its default gateway 20.1.1.1 (r1 eth4). R1 holds a correct OSPF route for 120.0.0.0/8 learned via 111.1.1.2 (r11 eth1). R11 is the EIGRP-to-OSPF boundary router: it participates in EIGRP AS 100 with r12 over the 112.0.0.0/8 segment (EE domain), learns r12's advertisement of 120.0.0.0/8 via EIGRP, and redistributes it into OSPF area 3. R12 is intentionally EIGRP-only (no ospf stanza), so the OSPF snapshot's "no network statements" flag is by design, not a fault. R13 and r8's OSPF anomalies are similarly benign: r13 is EIGRP-only, and r8 is the sole ABR for a valid single-device stub area (0.0.0.2), with Full adjacencies in area 0.0.0.1 and the backbone virtual link confirmed up.

Phase A (infra_sweep, l2_snapshot) found no ACL rules, no duplicate MACs, no ARP poisoning, and no link faults. Phase B (ospf_snapshot, tc_snapshot) confirmed all path-relevant adjacencies full and no traffic shaping. Phase D (pressure_sweep) found no stressed or crashed devices. No flap script, no carrier-change history, and no syslog evidence of a past failure mechanism exist.

Root cause: The reported connectivity outage is unconfirmed — the network is healthy and no fault trace exists.

Fix: No corrective action required. Advise the user to re-test from PC0; if the issue recurs, capture the exact error output and timestamp so a transient event can be correlated with lab logs.
